description: How self-interested and cooperating agents decide, bargain, compete and learn together: game theory, mechanism design, auctions, voting, negotiation, multi-agent reinforcement learning and collective behaviour. Students compute equilibria, run tournaments and simulations of agent populations, and critique recent research.
modelledOn: Shoham and Leyton-Brown, Multiagent Systems: Algorithmic, Game-Theoretic and Logical Foundations
Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory
Wooldridge, An Introduction to MultiAgent Systems
outcomes: Model strategic situations as normal-form and extensive-form games and compute dominant, Nash, subgame-perfect and correlated equilibria.
Design mechanisms and auctions that give agents incentives to report truthfully, and prove or refute their incentive properties.
Analyse voting, matching and fair-division rules against axioms and known impossibility results.
Implement negotiation, task-allocation and argumentation protocols for cooperating software agents.
Train and evaluate agents in multi-agent reinforcement learning settings, and explain failures such as non-stationarity and social dilemmas.
Simulate collective behaviour and critique recent multi-agent research with respect to evaluation, robustness and ethics.

units.title: Agents and rational choice
topics: Agent architectures: reactive, deliberative, BDI and layered
Utility theory: preferences, the von Neumann-Morgenstern axioms and risk attitudes
Environment properties and multi-agent settings
Decision-theoretic agents: expected utility and Markov decision processes
Agent communication: speech acts, FIPA-ACL and ontologies

units.title: Normal-form games
topics: Strategic games, dominance and iterated elimination of dominated strategies
Nash equilibrium and best response; existence by fixed-point theorems
Mixed strategies, support enumeration and the Lemke-Howson algorithm for bimatrix games
Zero-sum games, the minimax theorem and its LP formulation
Correlated and coarse correlated equilibrium; price of anarchy
Classic games: prisoner's dilemma, stag hunt, chicken and battle of the sexes

units.title: Extensive-form, repeated and evolutionary games
topics: Game trees, perfect and imperfect information and information sets
Backward induction and subgame-perfect equilibrium; minimax with alpha-beta pruning
Sequence-form representation and Bayesian games; Bayes-Nash equilibrium
Repeated games: the folk theorem, grim trigger, tit-for-tat and discounting
Evolutionary game theory: evolutionarily stable strategies and replicator dynamics
Learning in games: fictitious play, regret matching and convergence to coarse correlated equilibrium

units.title: Mechanism design
topics: Social choice, dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and the revelation principle
The VCG mechanism, Clarke pivot rule and Groves mechanisms
Optimal mechanisms: virtual valuations and revenue maximisation
Impossibility results: Arrow's theorem and the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
Budget balance, individual rationality and algorithmic mechanism design

units.title: Auctions, voting and matching
topics: Auction formats: English, Dutch, first-price and second-price; revenue equivalence
Bidding equilibria; private versus common values and the winner's curse
Combinatorial and multi-unit auctions; winner determination and spectrum auctions
Voting rules: plurality, Borda, Condorcet methods, approval and single transferable vote; manipulation
Matching markets: stable matching and the Gale-Shapley algorithm; school and organ allocation
Cooperative games and fair division: the core, the Shapley value and bargaining

units.title: Coordination, negotiation and argumentation
topics: Coordination: conventions, focal points, social laws and task allocation by contract net
Distributed constraint optimisation: ADOPT and DPOP
Negotiation: alternating-offers bargaining, monotonic concession protocol and automated negotiation strategies
Argumentation: abstract argumentation frameworks, grounded and preferred semantics and dialogue games
Coalition formation and teamwork with joint intentions

units.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning
topics: Stochastic games and MARL settings: cooperative, competitive and mixed
Independent Q-learning and the non-stationarity problem
Centralised training with decentralised execution: MADDPG and QMIX value decomposition
Self-play, population-based training and opponent modelling
Learning to communicate and emergent protocols
Credit assignment and sequential social dilemmas

units.title: Swarm and collective behaviour
topics: Flocking, consensus protocols and convergence via the graph Laplacian
Ant colony and particle swarm optimisation
Stigmergy, self-organisation and agent-based modelling
Opinion dynamics and the wisdom of crowds: DeGroot model, voter model and epidemic spread on networks
Agent-based simulation of a market of traders or minibus routes

units.title: Evaluation, ethics and research project
topics: Designing a multi-agent system for a real problem: mobile-money fraud, traffic or irrigation
Evaluating multi-agent systems: welfare, exploitability and robustness
Ethics and safety of multi-agent AI, including collusion in algorithmic pricing
Reading and critiquing recent papers; open problems

schedule.title: Agents, utility and communication
schedule.exercise: Specify the architecture, environment properties and utility function for a cooperative fleet of delivery agents and defend the design.

tasks.title: Classify the environment of three agent tasks by observability, determinism, dynamics and number of agents and note the effect on design
Solve a small Markov decision process by value iteration, stepping through the sweeps and reading off the optimal policy
Elicit a risk-averse utility function from a set of lottery choices, fit a curve in code and predict the choice in a new lottery

schedule.title: Dominance and Nash equilibrium
schedule.exercise: Find all pure and mixed Nash equilibria of six small games by hand and check each with a program that tests best responses.

tasks.title: Apply iterated elimination of dominated strategies to a 3 by 3 game and identify the surviving outcome
Write a program that finds all pure Nash equilibria of any two-player game matrix and test it on five games
Implement support enumeration for bimatrix games and use it to find the mixed equilibrium of a three-strategy game with verification

schedule.title: Zero-sum games, correlated equilibrium and classics
schedule.exercise: Solve a zero-sum security game with linear programming and compute the price of anarchy for a routing game.

tasks.title: Play prisoner's dilemma, stag hunt and chicken against scripted agents and record which strategy earns most in each
Solve a rock-paper-scissors-style zero-sum game as a linear programme and confirm the value equals the minimax value
Compute the price of anarchy of a Pigou-style two-road network and compare a correlated equilibrium with the best Nash payoff

schedule.title: Game trees and Bayesian games
schedule.exercise: Solve a sequential bargaining game by backward induction and find the Bayes-Nash equilibrium of a sealed-bid game with private costs.

tasks.title: Run backward induction on a game tree with four decision nodes and mark the subgame-perfect path
Apply minimax with alpha-beta pruning to a given tree, count the nodes pruned and compare with the plain minimax count
Derive the Bayes-Nash equilibrium bidding strategy for a first-price auction with two uniform bidders and plot it against the simulation

schedule.title: Repeated, evolutionary and learning dynamics
schedule.exercise: Run a tournament of repeated-game strategies, then show replicator dynamics and regret matching converging in a population.

tasks.title: Play tit-for-tat, grim trigger and always-defect against each other for 100 rounds and tabulate the average payoffs
Simulate replicator dynamics for hawk-dove and identify the evolutionarily stable mixed strategy from the trajectory
Implement regret matching for two players in a repeated game and show that the empirical play converges to a coarse correlated equilibrium

schedule.title: Mechanism design and impossibility results
schedule.exercise: Design a mechanism for allocating a public good, prove its truthfulness and compute the VCG payments for a worked example.

tasks.title: Compute VCG payments for three bidders competing for two items and verify that each bidder pays the externality they impose
Test by brute force over all value profiles whether a given allocation and payment rule is dominant-strategy truthful
Construct a profile showing that a given voting rule violates a fairness axiom, and relate the counterexample to Arrow's theorem

schedule.title: Auctions and bidding
schedule.exercise: Simulate first- and second-price auctions with learning bidders, compare seller revenue, and solve a small combinatorial winner determination problem.

tasks.title: Simulate 10,000 second-price auctions with random valuations and show that bidding the true value is never worse
Simulate a common-value auction with noisy signals and measure how often the winner loses money when bidders ignore the winner's curse
Solve winner determination for a spectrum auction with package bids as an integer programme and verify the result by brute force

schedule.title: Voting, matching and fair division
schedule.exercise: Compare voting rules on one preference profile, run a stable matching for students and schools, and divide a resource using the Shapley value.

tasks.title: Apply plurality, Borda and Condorcet rules to one set of ranked ballots and note the different winners
Step through the Gale-Shapley algorithm for six students and three schools and check that the result has no blocking pair
Compute Shapley values for a four-player cost-sharing game by enumeration and test whether the allocation lies in the core

schedule.title: Coordination, negotiation and argumentation
schedule.exercise: Build agents that negotiate over price and delivery, and evaluate their strategies against each other in a tournament.

tasks.title: Step through a contract net auction among four agents allocating five tasks and record each bid and award
Implement an alternating-offers negotiation with two concession strategies and compare the agreement rates and utilities over 100 runs
Compute the grounded and preferred extensions of an argumentation framework of ten arguments and explain how a new argument changes them

schedule.title: Multi-agent learning basics
schedule.exercise: Train independent learners in a cooperative grid task, observe the instability, and compare with a value-decomposition method.

tasks.title: Watch two Q-learning agents in a matrix game and describe how each agent's policy changes while the other agent also learns
Train independent Q-learners on a two-agent coordination grid and plot the success rate against episodes over ten seeds
Implement a simple value decomposition network, compare it with independent learners on the same task and analyse credit assignment

schedule.title: Self-play, communication and social dilemmas
schedule.exercise: Train competing and communicating agents, and analyse a sequential social dilemma in which cooperation collapses.

tasks.title: Train a self-play agent for a small board game and track its win rate against a fixed random opponent
Train two agents with a one-symbol channel on a referential game and inspect the meaning that emerges
Run a resource-harvesting dilemma with independent learners, show over-exploitation, and test a reward-shaping fix measured by total welfare

schedule.title: Swarms, opinion dynamics and agent-based models
schedule.exercise: Build an agent-based model of minibus drivers choosing routes and show how consensus and opinion spread across a network.

tasks.title: Simulate a consensus protocol on a ring of eight agents and plot the convergence of their values to the average
Use ant colony optimisation on a 12-city tour and compare its best tour with that found by a nearest-neighbour heuristic
Build an agent-based simulation of 200 drivers choosing between two routes and find whether congestion converges to the Nash equilibrium

schedule.title: Project, evaluation, ethics and research critique
schedule.exercise: Present a multi-agent design for a real problem with evaluation results, an ethics review and a critique of one recent paper.

tasks.title: Work a case on algorithmic pricing agents that learn to collude, listing the harms and the safeguards you would require
Evaluate a trained multi-agent policy by measuring its welfare and its exploitability against a best-response opponent
Implement and test the project multi-agent system, vary the number of agents and report how welfare and robustness scale
